subject: Clarifying order-form & SLA addendum: regional latency tiers, failover credits, and evidence path
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healz.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: mark.liao@healz.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA addendum & order-form language — regional latency tiers and failover credits

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the integration, our legal and SRE teams asked whether Redwood can provide a tailored SLA addendum that: 1) defines regional latency tiers (P95 / P99 by region), 2) specifies failover credit calculations when cross-region failover is used, and 3) includes an exhibit listing the operational evidence you can deliver (monthly availability reports, incident timelines, and the KV-cache hit rate summaries we've discussed).

We attached a short outline of what Healz would need as an initial ask (attached). Can you confirm:
- whether Redwood can accept per-region P95/P99 commitments with different credit bands?
- how you calculate credits for cross-region failover (do you prorate by impacted region or apply a global blended metric?)
- what evidence formats you can provide and whether those are sufficient for procurement (CSV/Excel exports, SOC2 attestations, and a runbook snapshot)?

We're working toward a contract signature window in mid-September; if needed, we can accept an addendum + order-form language that references a future evidence onboarding checklist.

Appreciate a quick call or a short redline we can push to procurement.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Ops, Healz, Inc.
attachments: proposed-sla-outline.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healz.com>
Cc: mark.liao@healz.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum & order-form language — regional latency tiers and failover credits

Elena —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. We can definitely work with per-region latency tiers; our platform supports region-specific telemetry and we can express P95 and P99 in the addendum. A few clarifications so we give you a clean draft:

1) Failover credit calculation: our standard approach is to measure availability per-region and apply credits for the impacted region only. For cross-region failover events where traffic is routed to an alternate region, we can offer two options:
   - Regional-prorated credits (default): credits calculated against the impacted region's SLA band.
   - Blended credits (optional): a blended calculation across affected regions (requires agreement on weighting).

2) Evidence you can expect: monthly region-by-region availability CSV, incident timeline PDF for Sev1/Sev2 within 72 hours after incident closure, and a summary CSV of cache-hit rates per model variant. We can also provide SOC 2 Type II report on request (redaction rules apply).

3) Order-form language: we'll provide a draft SLA addendum document plus an "Order Form Exhibit" that lists the covered regions, model families, and the credit schedule. That exhibit can be attached to the MSA or SOW.

Next steps I propose: I will circulate an initial draft addendum and a short evidence matrix. Can Kimberly and David weigh in on whether the evidence formats above match procurement expectations (kimberly) and whether ops can provide the cache and telemetry exports as CSV (david)?

I'm putting a tentative DocuSign path in the draft to avoid back-and-forth on signature routing. Will flag any items that must be escalated to legal.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-sla-addendum_v1.docx, evidence-matrix.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healz.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum & order-form language — regional latency tiers and failover credits

Priyom / David —

Couple of procurement notes from my side:
- Healz will expect the addendum to reference the active Order Form by ID and to include a definitions section for "Region" and "Failover" to avoid ambiguity.
- We should include an evidence onboarding timeline: e.g., SOC2 request turnaround (typically 10 business days), monthly availability report template to be delivered within 5 business days of month end, and incident timelines delivered within 3 business days of closure as Priyom suggested.
- For credits: the regional-prorated default is fine, but provide the blended calculation as an opt-in clause (Customer may request blended calculation by written notice).

David — can we confirm what exports the platform can produce today? Specifically: availability_by_region.csv, cache_hit_summary.csv (per model tag), and incident_report_template.pdf. If ops can produce those within the timeline, we can attach them as examples in the evidence-matrix.

I'll also prepare a redline of the order-form exhibit language so legal has fewer comments.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: orderform-redlines.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healz.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum & order-form language — regional latency tiers and failover credits

Kim / Priyom / Elena —

Confirming ops can produce the following:
- availability_by_region.csv (daily snapshots; monthly rollup provided as CSV)
- cache_hit_summary.csv (per model family, hourly, aggregated to monthly on request)
- incident_report_template.pdf (we populate incident timelines; available within 72 hours after incident closure)

On the timeline: we can support the evidence onboarding within 10 business days of contract signature for the standard reports. For SOC2, we will provide a redacted report within 10 business days of signed NDA if Healz requests it for procurement review.

I'll loop Grace for any regional telemetry caveats — some APAC regions have slightly different metric names, but since Healz is US-first we should be fine.

Elena — happy to set a 30-minute alignment call next week to walk through the draft addendum and the example CSVs.

-David
David Kim
Director, Site Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
